answer: Ledger-Anchored Coordination Windows. Each agent identity must publish a signed coordination manifest before it can be counted in any quorum; manifests are timestamped on a shared mesa of append-only checkpoints, and two manifests sharing an opal fingerprint (device, key lineage, timing signature) collapse into one voting weight. An attacker wanting N effective identities must sustain N distinct fingerprint lineages across successive windows, paying the full compute and key-ceremony cost per lineage, and any identity that skips a window forfeits its ledge and restarts at zero seniority.
